subject: OrionFence onboarding: access controls sprint & ops runbook
messages:

Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding - access controls sprint?

Diego / Redwood team —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team asked me to follow up with a practical plan for SSO, SCIM and IP allowlisting during the POC. We have two goals: (1) finish SSO + SCIM provisioning for 120 users, and (2) lock down API-level egress via IP allowlist for the staging environment.

Can you share a short ops checklist and confirm what information you need from our side this week? Also, what is the expected window to enable SCIM sync once we provide service account credentials?

Attachments: none

—Alex
Alex Tran
IT Engineering Manager, OrionFence
alex.tran@orionfence.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding - access controls sprint?

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. High-level answers up front:
- SSO (SAML) can be validated in a staging cutover within 48–72 hours after we receive your SAML metadata and a test user.
- SCIM provisioning typically takes 1–3 business days to configure and smoke-test for groups of this size once we have a service account with SCIM write scope and a mapping sheet.
- IP allowlist for our ingestion endpoints can be configured immediately on our side; we’ll need the maintainable CIDR ranges you plan to use and a staging egress IP (or VPCE).

I attached a short ops playbook and a SCIM mapping template — these are starting points. Proposed next steps:
1) You share SAML metadata + single test user by EOD Monday (Jun 14).
2) We provision a staging SAML connector + run a smoke test (48–72h).
3) You provide a service account for SCIM with the least privilege, and the completed mapping template.
4) We enable IP allowlist in staging and confirm connectivity.

I’m looping in Monica (CS lead) and Marissa (implementation PM) below to coordinate the work windows and runbook updates.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-access-playbook-v1.pdf; scim-mapping-template.xlsx

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding - access controls sprint?

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks — this is great, and the windows work for us. A few clarifications and the operational guardrails we apply:

Operational guardrails (short):
- SCIM idempotency: our SCIM worker uses externalId and email as primary keys; duplicates are avoided if externalId is present. If duplicates occur, our rollback is to pause provisioning, run a reconciliation job and apply a fix using the exported user map.
- IdP consent: we don’t need org-level admin consent in most SAML IdPs to test SSO; for full group-push across your org we need the SCIM service account to have group write permissions. We’ll call out the exact scopes in the mapping template.
- Change window & monitoring: during the first pass we run provisioning with a 10-user pilot group, monitor logs for 4 hours, then scale to the full set.

Planned sequence (we will execute):
1) Tue 10:00 PT: Redwood config SAML connector in staging + test access with your test user.
2) Tue 12:00 PT: Kick off SCIM pilot (10 users) using scim-redwood@orionfence.com.
3) Tue 14:00 PT: Validate logs & roll forward to full 120-user sync or rollback if any critical errors.

Action items for OrionFence (from this thread):
- Share SCIM API key in vault and confirm SCIM service account scope (Priya).
- Confirm single test user for SSO (Alex).
- Confirm any additional staging CIDRs if different from the sample (Priya).

I’m adding a short runbook checklist to the drive link and will update it after the pilot.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
